claim.why_it_matters: 8.4.3.1.2 General format is the identifier general-format figure. The Format 3 label is glued onto the end of the Format 2 general-format skeleton line, so the transcription reads as though the Format 2 skeleton were 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):' and Format 3 has no label of its own -- the skeleton 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1' at the top of page 155 is left orphaned with no format heading. Anyone deriving the identifier formats from the markdown loses the Format 2 / Format 3 boundary. The label is also on the wrong side of the page-155 anchor (it is printed at the top of page 155, not the bottom of 154).

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages at 300 dpi. PDF page 154 (printed page 124) ends section 8.4.3.1.2 with exactly three blocks after the 'General format' heading: 'Format 1 (function-identifier):' / 'function-identifier-1' / 'Format 2 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts):' / 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1'. Nothing follows that last skeleton on page 154 except the folio '124 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license footer -- there is NO 'Format 3' label anywhere on page 154. PDF page 155 (printed page 125) opens, directly under the running head, with 'Format 3 (reference-modification):' on its own line, then 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1', then Formats 4 through 11. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 6678) reads 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):' as a single line, positioned two lines BEFORE the anchor at line 6680, with 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1' appearing alone at line 6685 after the anchor and the repeated running head. Both halves of the claim hold: (a) the Format 3 heading is joined to the Format 2 skeleton with no intervening blank line, and (b) it is attributed to page 154 when the PDF prints it at the top of page 155. This is not mere page-break furniture or line wrapping -- in a general-format figure the block boundary between a 'Format N (...):' label and its skeleton IS the content. As transcribed, a reader or extractor taking the line after 'Format 2 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts):' gets a two-clause line that is not a valid skeleton, and taking the line after 'Format 3 (reference-modification):' gets a blank line and a page anchor rather than 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1'. The Format 2 / Format 3 boundary in the identifier general format is genuinely corrupted. No characters are lost or altered, so this is a block-structure and page-attribution defect rather than dropped text; severity 'structural' is apt.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with a precision note. No text is missing or misspelled -- every word of both formats survives. The defect is twofold: (1) block merge -- the paragraph break between the Format 2 skeleton and the Format 3 label is lost, producing the single markdown line 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:6678), which destroys the label-to-skeleton pairing for both Format 2 and Format 3 in the 8.4.3.1.2 identifier general format; and (2) page misattribution -- that Format 3 label is placed before the anchor (line 6680), i.e. transcribed as page-154 content, whereas the PDF prints it as the first line of body text on page 155 (printed page 125), immediately above 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1'. PDF page 154 (printed 124) genuinely ends at 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1'. Fix: split line 6678 into 'qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1' on its own line, and move 'Format 3 (reference-modification):' to after the page-155 anchor and running head, immediately preceding 'identifier-1 reference-modifier-1' at line 6685.
